notes: Breadboard naming follows the catalogue: the image's upper half (rows f-j) is bank 'b', the lower half (rows a-e) is bank 't'. The sensor sits in columns 1-4 of row j.

Echo path: Echo (3b) -> blue wire -> 4t.d -> 330 ohm (4t.c to 8t.c) -> column 8 junction -> 470 ohm (8t.b to 12t.b) -> wire to ground rail. GPIO17 is tapped from the 330/470 junction (8t.e), so the Pi sees about 5 V x 470/800 = 2.9 V, safe for 3.3 V logic.
Pi pins from the image: red to 5V (physical pin 2 = 5V.1), green to GP4 (pin 7), blue to GP17 (pin 11), black to GND at pin 39 (GND.8).
Ground rail hole numbers (bn.12, bn.24, bn.28) are read from the image's column positions; the rail is one strip so the exact numbers do not change the connectivity.
The manual says Trig can use any GPIO and Echo any GPIO; GPIO4 and GPIO17 are what the image shows.
